q: What did the servant the king forgave do to a fellow servant who owed him a hundred denarii?
a: Grabbed him and began to choke him

q: What question about marriage did the Pharisees ask to test Jesus?
a: Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?

q: What was Jesus teaching about when he said, “Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate”?
a: Marriage

q: How long is the marriage tie binding?
a: Until one of the married persons dies.

q: What question did the rich young man first ask Jesus in Matthew 19:16?
a: "Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?"

q: In Matthew 19:24, Jesus said it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for what to happen?
a: A rich man entering the kingdom of God

q: What two questions did the disciples and Peter ask Jesus before He told the story of the workers in the vineyard?
a: "Who can be saved?" and "What will there be for us?"

q: What reward did Jesus say the twelve apostles would get for forsaking everything and following him?
a: You will sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel

q: In the parable of the workers in the vineyard, what did the landowner agree to pay the workers he hired early in the morning for the day?
a: A denarius

q: In which parable do workers hired at the end of the day receive the same wage as those hired at dawn?
a: The Workers in the Vineyard

q: In Jesus' story of the workers in the vineyard, at what other hours did the landowner go out to hire more workers?
a: The third, sixth, ninth and eleventh hours

q: In Jesus' parable of the workers in the vineyard, how did the owner tell his foreman to pay the workers in the evening?
a: Starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first

q: What is eternal death?
a: A dreadful state of separation from God and everlasting anguish and suffering in hell

q: In Jesus' parable of the workers in the vineyard, what did the landowner say when the original workers grumbled about the pay?
a: “Or are you envious because I am generous?”

q: In Matthew 20, as Jesus went up to Jerusalem and told the twelve disciples what would happen to Him, who would first condemn the Son of Man to death?
a: The chief priests and scribes

q: What did James’ and John’s mother ask of Jesus?
a: For her sons to sit on Jesus' right and left

q: Whom has God given power to declare the forgiveness of sins?
a: The congregation, through its ministers. [Absolution.]

q: In Matthew 20, when Jesus told the brothers that He would drink a cup and asked if they could drink it, what did James and John answer?
a: “We can”

q: What comfort is it to you that Christ will come to judge the living and the dead?
a: Christ, who bore God's judgment for me, will judge my enemies and bring me to glory.

q: After the children shouted praise to Jesus in the temple courts, where did He go to spend the night?
a: At Bethany

q: In the last week before his death, at what town near Jerusalem did Jesus spend the night?
a: At Bethany

q: Which miracle did Jesus perform on a tree that had leaves but no fruit?
a: Cursing the fig tree

q: When the chief priests and elders challenged Jesus in the temple courts, what question did Jesus ask them in return?
a: Whether John’s baptism was from heaven or from men

q: In Matthew 21, why did the chief priests and elders refuse to say that John’s baptism was from men?
a: They were afraid of the people, who regarded John as a prophet

q: In which parable does one son say he will not work but does, while the other agrees but does not go?
a: The Two Sons

q: In Jesus' parable of the two sons, whom did Jesus say were entering the kingdom of God ahead of the chief priests and elders because they believed John?
a: The tax collectors and prostitutes

q: In which parable do tenant farmers mistreat and kill the vineyard owner's servants and finally kill his son?
a: The Wicked Tenants

q: In Jesus' parable of the wicked tenants, what did the landowner build in his vineyard besides a wall and a winepress?
a: A tower

q: In Jesus' story, what did the tenants do when the vineyard owner sent his servants to collect his share of the fruit?
a: They beat and killed the servants

q: In Jesus' parable, what did the tenants do when the landowner sent his own son to collect the fruit?
a: They threw him out of the vineyard and killed him

q: In the parable of the wicked tenants, why did the tenants say they would kill the landowner's son?
a: To take his inheritance

q: In Jesus' story, what did the people say the vineyard owner would do with his vineyard after dealing with the wicked tenants?
a: Rent it to other tenants who would give him his share of the fruit

q: After the parable of the wicked tenants, what did Jesus say would be taken away from the chief priests and Pharisees and given to a people who would produce its fruit?
a: The kingdom of God

q: In Matthew 22:1-14, what parable did Jesus tell in the temple about a king and his son?
a: The Wedding Feast.

q: In Jesus' parable of the wedding banquet, after the invited guests were not worthy, whom did the servants gather in from the streets?
a: Everyone they could find, both evil and good

q: In Jesus' story of the wedding feast, where did the invited people go instead of coming?
a: To their fields and their businesses

q: Whom did the king spot among the guests at the wedding banquet?
a: A man not dressed in wedding clothes

q: In the parable of the wedding feast, where did the king order the servants to throw the man who was not dressed in wedding clothes?
a: Into the outer darkness

q: In Jesus' story of the wedding feast, what did the king do to the man who had no wedding clothes?
a: Had him thrown into the darkness

q: What are a Christian's duties to his country?
a: Obey laws, be patriotic, pray, defend it, pay taxes, vote conscientiously.

q: Which Christian doctrine did the Sadducees reject?
a: Resurrection

q: When Jesus answered the Sadducees about the resurrection, what did He say people will be like in the resurrection?
a: They will be like the angels in heaven

q: On how many commandments does Jesus say all the Law and the Prophets hang?
a: Two

q: Does God's Law demand outward observance only?
a: No; it demands the whole man, and the willing obedience of heart and mind

q: What is the substance of the first table?
a: Love of God

q: Why is the First Commandment called the Great Commandment?
a: Because it includes all the rest; obedience to all must proceed from the love of God it requires.

q: What is the substance of the second table?
a: Love to our neighbor

q: May we love ourselves?
a: Yes, for God has made us, but we must beware of selfishness

q: In Jesus' question about the Christ, how did He say David called the Christ 'Lord'?
a: In the Spirit

q: When in particular did he suffer this anguish?
a: In the garden of Gethsemane and on the cross, crying "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?"

q: In Matthew 23, Jesus said the scribes and Pharisees sit in whose seat, so that the people should practice what they tell them?
a: Moses’ seat

q: Why shouldn’t we call anyone on earth “Father”?
a: We have one Father, who is in heaven

q: In Jesus’ woe about winning a convert, what did the scribes and Pharisees make the convert become?
a: Twice as much a son of hell as they were

q: Jesus accused the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, of paying tithes of mint, dill, and cumin while disregarding which weightier matters of the law?
a: Justice, mercy, and faithfulness

q: In Matthew 23, Jesus compared the scribes and Pharisees to what, which look beautiful outside but are full of dead men’s bones inside?
a: Whitewashed tombs

q: In Matthew 23, Jesus said the blood of the righteous would come upon that generation, from the blood of Abel to the blood of which man, murdered between the temple and the altar?
a: Zechariah son of Berechiah

q: When Jesus spoke of righteous people killed long ago, whose name did He say first?
a: Abel

q: In Matthew 23, after Jesus said Jerusalem was unwilling to be gathered, what did He say would be left to her desolate?
a: Her house

q: What are we to believe concerning the resurrection?
a: General resurrection of just and unjust; living changed in moment; bodies raised and united to souls; just in power and incorruption

q: When Jesus' disciples pointed out the temple buildings, what did Jesus say would happen to the stones of the temple?
a: Not one stone would be left on another

q: On the Mount of Olives, the disciples asked Jesus to tell them the sign of what?
a: His coming and of the end of the age

q: In Jesus' teaching on the end of the age in Matthew 24, what will happen to the love of most people because of the multiplication of wickedness?
a: It will grow cold

q: In Matthew 24, when Jesus' hearers see 'the abomination of desolation' standing in the holy place, where does He say those in Judea should flee?
a: To the mountains

q: In Matthew 24, Jesus tells His disciples to pray that their flight will not occur in the winter or on which day?
a: On the Sabbath

q: In Matthew 24:24, Jesus warns that false christs and false prophets will rise up and perform great signs and wonders. What is their aim?
a: To deceive, if possible, even the elect

q: According to Matthew 24:36, who alone knows the day and hour of Christ's return?
a: God the Father

q: Jesus said what people were doing before the flood, until the day Noah went into the ark. What were they doing?
a: Eating, drinking and getting married

q: What two important things has God revealed to us about the Last Day?
a: It will come suddenly when nobody expects it, and it will come soon.

q: Which parable primarily teaches believers to stay spiritually ready and watchful for Christ's return?
a: The Ten Virgins

q: In Matthew 25:13, at the end of the parable of the ten virgins, what does Jesus tell His followers to do, since they do not know the day or the hour?
a: Keep watch

q: In the parable of the talents, what did the master say the servant with one talent should have done with the money?
a: Deposited it with the bankers to earn interest

q: In which teaching of Jesus does the King say, "whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me"?
a: The Sheep and the Goats

q: In Matthew 25:31, when the Son of Man comes in His glory with all the angels, what will He do?
a: He will sit on His glorious throne.

q: When the Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, who will be gathered before Him?
a: All the people of the world

q: Where do all the risen go after the day of judgment?
a: The chosen enter into life everlasting; the condemned, into eternal death

q: In the judgment, what will the King say to those on His right, who have done His will?
a: "Come, you who are blessed by My Father."

q: How is serving our neighbor the same as serving God?
a: Jesus taught that what we do to our neighbors for His sake, we do to Him.

q: When Jesus comes to judge the world, where will He send those who would not obey Him?
a: Away from Him, into eternal punishment

q: In Jesus' story, whom was the eternal fire prepared for?
a: The devil and his angels

q: What will the King say to those on His left?
a: "Depart from Me, you who are cursed."

q: In Jesus' teaching about the sheep and the goats, where did Jesus say the people who did not help others would go?
a: Away to be punished forever

q: What does Jesus say will happen at the end to the wicked and to the righteous?
a: Wicked to punishment, righteous to eternal life

q: How long does Jesus say the punishment of the wicked will last?
a: Forever

q: What does Jesus say will happen to sinners who are not saved?
a: They will be punished forever.

q: What punishment awaits sinners after their death?
a: Eternal damnation.

q: What is hell?
a: A place of dreadful and endless torment.

q: What difference is there between the Lord's supper and the papal mass?
a: Supper witnesses complete forgiveness through Christ's one sacrifice; mass wrongly teaches daily re-offering and worship of Christ bodily present in bread.

q: In Matthew 26, when Jesus finished teaching and spoke to His disciples, how many days away did He say the Passover was?
a: Two days away

q: When the chief priests and elders gathered in the courtyard of Caiaphas and plotted against Jesus, why did they say they should not arrest Him during the feast?
a: There might be a riot among the people

q: When a woman poured perfume on Him, what did Jesus say she had done?
a: "She has done a beautiful deed to Me."

q: When Jesus was anointed at Simon the Leper's home in Bethany, what did He say the woman had prepared by pouring perfume on Him?
a: His body for burial

q: According to Matthew 26:15, what did the chief priests set out for Judas Iscariot to betray Jesus?
a: Thirty pieces of silver

q: How many pieces of silver did Judas receive for betraying Jesus?
How can bodily eating and drinking do such great things?
a: Not the eating and drinking, but the words and faith in them, give forgiveness of sins

q: How does the Lord's Supper strengthen our faith and assure us of forgiveness of sins, life, and salvation?
a: Christ gives us His body and blood, by which He purchased forgiveness of sins, strengthening our faith in Him

q: Which name for the Sacrament of the Altar means "thanksgiving"?
a: Eucharist (meaning thanksgiving)

q: From what do we learn what the Lord's Supper is?
a: From the words of Christ Himself as given by Matthew, Mark, Luke, and St. Paul.

q: Where in the words of institution are the benefits of the Lord's Supper pointed out?
a: In these words: 'poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.'

q: What personal assurance does each communicant receive in the Lord's Supper?
a: Christ's body was given and His blood poured out for him, for the forgiveness of his sins.

q: What gives the Lord's Supper the power to confer such great benefits as forgiveness and salvation?
a: Christ's Word of promise joined to the bread and wine

q: What benefit do we have from the Lord's Supper?
a: Through the words 'given and poured out for you for the forgiveness of sins,' we receive forgiveness, life, and salvation

q: How can we be sure that life and salvation are given us in the Sacrament, even though Christ only mentions forgiveness of sins?
a: Where there is forgiveness of sins, there is also life and salvation

q: In Matthew 26, after telling His disciples they would all fall away, where did Jesus say He would go ahead of them after He had risen?
a: Into Galilee

q: Describe the sufferings of Christ.
a: His whole life was suffering; greatest sufferings in Gethsemane, before the council, and under Pontius Pilate

q: How should we pray when we experience suffering and trouble?
a: Pray 'Your will be done' and ask for strength to remain steadfast in His will

q: How can we be kept pure?
a: We must watch and pray, and avoid everything that awakens impure desires

q: According to Matthew 26:57, to the house of which high priest was Jesus led after His arrest?
a: Caiaphas

q: In Matthew 26:63, what did the high priest charge Jesus under oath by the living God to tell them?
a: Whether He is the Christ, the Son of God.

q: What kind of swearing is permitted?
a: Legal oaths of witness, innocence, allegiance, or office before a magistrate.

q: What did Judas do with the silver he was paid for handing Jesus over?
a: He threw it into the temple

q: In Matthew 27, what did the chief priests buy with the returned thirty pieces of silver after Judas left?
a: The potter’s field, as a burial place for foreigners

q: When the chief priests and elders accused Jesus before Pilate in Matthew 27, how did Jesus respond to the charges?
a: He gave no answer, not even to a single charge

q: Before Pilate, what did the chief priests and elders persuade the crowds to ask for?
a: Barabbas to be released and Jesus to be executed

q: When Pilate said he was not to blame for Jesus' death, what did the people answer?
a: They would take the blame

q: Who twisted together a crown of thorns and set it on Jesus' head to mock Him?
a: The governor's soldiers (Roman soldiers)

q: Where did the governor's soldiers take Jesus?
a: Into the Praetorium, the governor's palace

q: What was the color of the robe placed on Jesus by the soldiers?
a: Scarlet / Purple

q: What did the soldiers put in Jesus' right hand?
a: A staff

q: After the soldiers put a staff in Jesus' hand, what did they do?
a: Knelt down to make fun of Him

q: What was the name of the place where Jesus was crucified?
a: Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull

q: About what hour did Jesus cry out in a loud voice on the cross, just before He died?
a: About the ninth hour

q: What happened to the veil of the Temple at the moment Jesus died?
a: It was torn in two from top to bottom

q: What happened to the tombs when Jesus died?
a: They broke open and dead saints were raised

q: In Matthew 27:54, what did the centurion and those with him say after they saw the earthquake and all that had happened?
a: “Truly this was the Son of God.”

q: What was the name of the person who buried Jesus' body in his own new tomb?
a: Joseph of Arimathea

q: According to the New Testament, who obtained permission to take Jesus Christ's body down from the cross and place it in the tomb?
a: Joseph of Arimathea

q: What is Baptism?
a: New Testament ordinance instituted by Christ signifying fellowship in death and life.

q: Wherein do Baptism and the Lord's Supper differ from the other ordinances of God?
a: Specially instituted by Christ to represent and apply to believers benefits of the new covenant

q: Is Christ, then, not with us until the end of the world, as He has promised us?
a: By His divinity, majesty, grace, and Spirit Christ is never absent from us; by His human nature He is no longer on earth.

q: Wherein do the sacraments of baptism and the Lord's supper agree?
a: Both authored by God; spiritual part is Christ and his benefits; seals of same covenant; dispensed by gospel ministers only

q: After his resurrection, where did Jesus tell his disciples to go to meet him?
a: To Galilee

q: Who saw the risen Jesus soon after Mary had seen him?
a: Some other women

q: Who went into the city and reported to the chief priests all that had happened at the tomb?
a: Some of the guards who had watched the tomb.

q: After the chief priests met with the elders and formed a plan, what did they tell the guards at Jesus' tomb to say had happened to His body?
a: His disciples came by night and stole Him away while they slept

q: Where does Jesus claim to have all authority in heaven and on earth?
a: In Matthew 28:18, He says, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.”

q: Why are we safe when we live under our Lord's rule?
a: Because He is almighty God, with all authority in heaven and on earth

q: What are the outward and ordinary Means, whereby Christ communicateth to us the Benefits of Redemption?
a: His ordinances, especially the Word, Baptism, the Lord's Supper, and Prayer.

q: What do we mean when we say God is a trinity?
a: Three Persons—Father, Son, Spirit—each fully God, not one-third; there is only one God

q: What is the first ordinance of the church?
a: Believer's baptism: immersion beneath water in the name of the Trinity

q: Why is the church called universal?
a: Its object is to gather all nations and include all true believers of all times and places

q: What is God's command concerning Baptism?
a: It is given in the words of Christ in the last chapter of Matthew

q: In what is the water of Baptism comprehended?
a: God's command and His word

q: What are the words of God's command concerning baptism?
a: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

q: Who ordinarily administers Holy Baptism?
a: Pastors, the called ministers of Christ

q: In cases of necessity, who may and should administer baptism?
a: Every Christian

q: Whom did Christ command us to baptize?
a: All nations; all human beings, old and young, men and women.

q: Whom do we generally baptize?
a: Both those instructed in the faith and little children.

q: How did the Apostles' Creed originate?
a: It grew out of the baptismal formula and came down from the early centuries of the Church

q: What does the Apostles' Creed contain?
a: In three articles, a statement of what the Triune God has done and still does for us

q: How do we know there are three Persons in the Holy Trinity?
a: Christ commanded baptism in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and all three were revealed at His baptism

q: Why should infants be baptized?
a: They need God's grace, are part of Christ's command to baptize all nations, and apostles baptized whole families

q: Who appointed these sacraments?
a: The Lord Jesus Christ.

q: Where has Christ promised that He will wash us with His blood and Spirit as surely as we are washed with the water of baptism?
a: In the institution of baptism, a promise repeated where Scripture speaks of the washing of new birth

q: How is our risen and ascended Lord present with us?
a: He is with us invisibly in His Word and Gospel.

q: Which Gospel opens with the words, "This is the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God"?
a: Mark

q: What does the catechism teach about those baptized but without faith?
a: Without faith, baptism does not save; they lose the heavenly inheritance

q: What are the punishments of sin in the world to come?
a: Everlasting separation from God's comfortable presence and most grievous torments in soul and body, without intermission, in hell fire forever.

q: In the synagogue at Capernaum, how did the man with an unclean spirit address Jesus?
a: “the Holy One of God”

q: In Mark 1, when Jesus drove out many demons at Simon and Andrew's door, why would He not allow the demons to speak?
a: Because they knew who He was

q: When Simon and his companions found Jesus in the solitary place and said everyone was looking for Him, what reason did Jesus give for going on to the neighboring towns?
a: To preach there, for that is why He had come

q: Why had Jesus the right to forgive sins?
a: Because the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins

q: When Jesus forgave the sins of the paralytic let down through the roof to him, to what did the scribes object?
a: They thought only God could forgive sins

q: In Mark 2, when Jesus saw Levi sitting at the tax booth, whose son was Levi?
a: Alphaeus

q: What other name was Matthew the tax collector known by?
a: Levi

q: Whom did Jesus see as He was walking beside the sea?
a: Levi son of Alphaeus

q: In Mark 2, when people came to Jesus asking why His disciples did not fast, which two groups were described as often fasting?
a: John’s disciples and the Pharisees

q: In Jesus' illustration in Mark 2, what kind of patch does no one sew on an old garment?
a: A patch of unshrunk cloth

q: In Jesus' illustration in Mark 2, what is ruined when someone pours new wine into old wineskins?
a: Both the wine and the wineskins

q: What did Jesus say to the man with the withered hand?
a: "Stand up among us."

q: After healing the man's hand, where did Jesus go with His disciples?
a: To the sea

q: In Mark 3, why did Jesus ask His disciples to have a boat ready for Him?
a: So the crowd would not crush Him

q: In Mark 3, when the unclean spirits saw Jesus, what did they cry out as they fell down before Him?
a: “You are the Son of God!”

q: In Mark 3:21, when Jesus' family went out to take custody of Him, what did they say?
a: “He is out of His mind.”

q: In Mark 3, where had the scribes who accused Jesus of being possessed by Beelzebul come from?
a: Jerusalem

q: In Jesus' parable in Mark 3 about a strong man's house, what must someone do first before he can plunder the house?
a: Tie up the strong man

q: What is the only sin that cannot be forgiven?
a: Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit

q: In Mark 3, why did Jesus say that whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven?
a: They were saying, "He has an unclean spirit."

q: Whom did Jesus say are His mother and brothers?
a: Whoever does the will of God

q: In Jesus' parable of the sower in Mark 4, how much crop did the seed that fell on good soil produce?
a: Thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold

q: In Mark 4, when Jesus was alone with the Twelve and those around Him, what did He say had been given to them?
a: The mystery of the kingdom of God

q: In Mark 4, Jesus said that with the measure a person uses, what will happen?
a: It will be measured to you, and even more added

q: In Jesus' parable of the seed growing secretly in Mark 4, what is the kingdom of God said to be like?
a: A man who scatters seed on the ground

q: In Jesus' parable of the growing seed, what does the man do as soon as the grain is ripe?
a: He swings the sickle, because the harvest has come

q: What miracle did Jesus perform just before healing Legion of his unclean spirit?
a: Calming of the storm

q: What was the name of the demon-possessed man Jesus healed in the region of the Gerasenes?
a: Legion

q: Where was the country of Decapolis?
a: East of the Sea of Galilee

q: Why could no one keep the man from the tombs tied up?
a: He broke the chains and shackles

q: What did the man with the unclean spirit keep doing night and day in the tombs and mountains?
a: Crying out

q: In Mark 5, the man living in the tombs shouted to Jesus, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You before God not to torture me!” What name did he give when Jesus asked his name?
a: Legion

q: Why was the name "Legion" given for the unclean spirits in the man?
a: Because there were many of them

q: What was the man like after the demons left him?
a: Sitting, dressed, and in his right mind

q: What was wrong with the woman who touched Jesus' cloak?
a: She had bleeding for twelve years

q: When Jesus raised Jairus's daughter in Mark 5:41-42, what did the girl do at once?
a: She got up and began to walk around

q: According to Mark 6:3, which of these men was a brother of Jesus?
a: James

q: How many of Jesus’ sisters are named in the Bible?
a: None

q: When Jesus sent out the Twelve in Mark 6, what was the only thing He told them to take for the journey?
a: A staff

q: Why does the Holy Spirit call baptism the washing of new birth and renewal, and the washing away of sins?
a: God teaches blood and Spirit remove sins like water removes dirt, and assures us we're truly cleansed spiritually as bodily.
ref: 1 Cor 6:11; Titus 3:5; Rev 1:5; Rev 7:14; Mark 16:16; Acts 2:38; Rom 6:3-4; Gal 3:27; Acts 22:16; 1 Peter 3:21

q: In Mark 6, what did John the Baptist tell Herod that was not lawful for him?
a: To have his brother’s wife

q: In Mark 6, what did Herod do when he heard John’s words?
a: He was greatly perplexed, yet listened gladly

q: When Herod held a birthday banquet and Herodias’ daughter pleased his guests, what did Herod swear to give her?
a: Whatever she asked, up to half his kingdom

q: What did the daughter of Herodias do that pleased King Herod and his guests?
a: She danced

q: Why did Herod not refuse the request for John the Baptist’s head, though he was consumed with sorrow?
a: Because of his oaths and his guests

q: How did King Herod feel when the girl asked him to put John the Baptist to death?
a: He was very sad

q: Where was John the Baptist when King Herod had him put to death?
a: In the prison

q: Who gave the order that John the Baptist be put to death?
a: King Herod

q: What did John the Baptist's disciples do with his body?
a: They placed it in a tomb

q: In Mark 6, how did Jesus have the people sit down before He fed them?
a: In groups of hundreds and fifties

q: In Mark 6, after Jesus walked on the water and climbed into the boat, where did He and His disciples land and moor the boat?
a: Gennesaret

q: In Mark 7, what complaint did the Pharisees and scribes bring against Jesus' disciples?
a: They ate with defiled, unwashed hands

q: Why is immersion not the only valid mode of baptism?
a: The Greek word baptize means to wash, which can be done in more than one way

q: In Mark 7, what practice did Jesus say let a man avoid helping his father or mother by calling his property "Corban"?
a: Declaring his goods a gift devoted to God

q: When Jesus explained to His disciples in the house why food cannot defile a man, where did He say food goes instead of into the heart?
a: Into the stomach, and then it is eliminated

q: Which miracle of Jesus is this: Jesus puts His fingers in a man's ears and touches his tongue to heal him?
a: Healing the deaf and mute man

q: From the region of Tyre and Sidon, into what region did Jesus go, by way of the Sea of Galilee?
a: To the region of the Decapolis

q: What did Jesus sometimes do as part of His healing miracles?
a: He spit

q: In Mark 7:37, after Jesus healed a deaf man who had trouble speaking, what did the astonished people say about him?
a: "He has done all things well!"

q: What is the great difference between Christ's first coming and His second coming?
a: First in humility and poverty; second in great power and glory.

q: After Jesus fed the four thousand and dismissed the crowd, to which district did He go by boat with His disciples?
a: The district of Dalmanutha

q: In Mark 8, when the Pharisees came and argued with Jesus, what did they demand from Him in order to test Him?
a: A sign from heaven

q: In Mark 8, when the disciples crossed the lake with Jesus and had forgotten to take bread, how many loaves did they have with them in the boat?
a: One loaf

q: How many times did Jesus put His hands on the blind man at Bethsaida before the man could see everything clearly?
a: Two times

q: In Mark 8, after Peter said to Jesus, “You are the Christ,” what did Jesus do?
a: He warned them not to tell anyone about Him.

q: In Mark 8, when Jesus began to teach His disciples that the Son of Man must suffer, who did He say would reject Him?
a: The elders, chief priests, and scribes

q: When Jesus was transfigured on the high mountain in Mark 9, what did Peter offer to put up?
a: Three shelters, one each for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah

q: After coming down from the mountain, what did Peter, James, and John ask Jesus about the scribes?
a: Why the scribes say that Elijah must come first

q: A father in the crowd brought his son to Jesus. What was wrong with the boy?
a: A spirit kept him from talking

q: Who said, "I do believe; help my unbelief!" when asking Jesus to heal his son?
a: The father of a demon-possessed boy

q: When the disciples asked Jesus privately why they could not drive the deaf and mute spirit out of the boy, what did He say this kind can come out by?
a: Only by prayer

q: When Jesus and His disciples passed through Galilee, according to Mark 9, why did Jesus not want anyone to know where they were?
a: He was teaching His disciples

q: After Jesus told His disciples in Galilee that the Son of Man would be killed and rise, how did they respond to His statement?
a: They did not understand it and were afraid to ask Him

q: In Mark 9:49, with what does Jesus say everyone will be salted?
a: Fire

q: Can they who have never heard the gospel, and so know not Jesus Christ, nor believe in him, be saved by their living according to the light of nature?
a: No; salvation is in Christ alone, however diligently they live by the light of nature or their own religion.

q: In Mark 10:2, who came to test Jesus by asking whether it is lawful for a man to divorce his wife?
a: Pharisees

q: In Mark 10:30, along with houses, family and fields, what did Jesus say those who leave all for Him and the gospel will receive in this present age?
a: Persecutions

q: In Mark 10, as Jesus and His followers went up the road to Jerusalem, what was Jesus doing in relation to His disciples?
a: Walking ahead of them

q: In Mark 10, when Jesus told the Twelve what would happen in Jerusalem, to whom did He say the chief priests and scribes would deliver Him over after condemning Him to death?
a: The Gentiles

q: What was the name of James’ and John’s father?
a: Zebedee

q: In Mark 10:46, after Jesus left the land of Perea, what city did He and His disciples come to next?
a: Jericho

q: In Mark 11, what did Jesus tell his two disciples to say if anyone asked why they were untying the colt?
a: “The Lord needs it and will return it shortly.”

q: When Jesus reached the fig tree in leaf on the road from Bethany and found no fruit, why was there no fruit on it?
a: It was not the season for figs

q: When Jesus cleansed the temple courts in Jerusalem, what would He not allow anyone to do there?
a: Carry merchandise through them

q: After Jesus drove out the buyers and sellers and taught in the temple courts, what did the chief priests and scribes look for?
a: A way to kill Him

q: In Mark 11, when Jesus was walking in the temple courts after returning to Jerusalem, which leaders came up to Him and asked by what authority He did these things?
a: The chief priests, scribes, and elders

q: In Mark 11, when Jesus asked the religious leaders whether John's baptism was from heaven or from men, how did they finally answer Him?
a: "We do not know."

q: Which apostle, the brother of John, did King Herod put to death with the sword?
a: James son of Zebedee

q: In Jesus' parable of the wicked tenants in Mark 12, what did the tenants do to the first servant the owner sent to collect his share of the fruit?
a: They seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed

q: In Jesus' parable of the wicked tenants, what did the owner say when he sent his beloved son to the tenants?
a: “They will respect my son.”

q: In Jesus' parable of the wicked tenants, what did the owner of the vineyard do to the tenants and the vineyard after they killed his son?
a: He killed the tenants and gave the vineyard to others

q: At the end of the parable of the wicked tenants in Mark 12, what Scripture did Jesus ask the leaders if they had never read?
a: “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.”

q: In Mark 12, which two groups did the leaders send to Jesus to catch him in his words about paying taxes?
a: Some of the Pharisees and Herodians
